checks.reason: A caller outside the declared access policy received the synthetic private marker

findings.title: Private fixture readable by another user
findings.impact: A caller outside the declared owner-only access policy retrieved the private synthetic fixture. Assess the sensitivity of equivalent real records before final severity assignment.
reproduction: Use the original scoped plan and the two distinct test-user sessions.
Confirm the owner can GET /notes/owner-note and the synthetic marker matches.
Repeat the request as other; the same marker is returned.
evidence: Owner identity and second-user identity were successfully checked and differ.
Owner response contained the configured synthetic marker.
other response also contained that exact marker; response bodies and credentials were not saved.
findings.remediation: Enforce the intended owner or membership check on the server/database for this operation. Trace the actual policy before selecting a code change.
findings.retest: Rerun this plan against the same kind of private fixture. The owner must retain access; unauthorized callers must not receive it.

limitations: Only configured owner-only JSON read operations were probed; this is not a complete security assessment.
The operator must verify account roles, fixture ownership, target ownership, and environment isolation. Configuration cannot prove these facts.
HTTP denials and an empty collection are narrow observations, not proof that no other data leaked.
No app binary, device behavior, write authorization, subscriptions, rate-limit strength, or deployed/local parity was automatically tested.
Response bodies are never persisted. Keep the original plan and test fixture available for reproduction.
cleanup: The runner created no remote resources. Any separately seeded fixtures must be cleaned up using their recorded IDs.
